title: Month-End Close Checklist: A Step-by-Step Template
summary: A complete month-end close checklist template, organized by phase, the tasks most teams miss, and how AI agents run the close faster.
body_markdown:
The difference between a smooth close and a stressful one is usually not talent, it is organization. A good **month-end close checklist** turns the close from a scramble into a repeatable process: every task listed, owned, sequenced, and checked off. This guide gives you a complete month-end close checklist template, organized by phase, plus the tasks teams most often miss and how AI agents now run much of it.


For the bigger picture of how the close works, see our guide to the[month-end close process](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/month-end-close-process) . This article is the practical checklist.


## **Why use a month-end close checklist?**


- **Consistency.** The same steps happen every period, so nothing is forgotten.
- **Accountability.** Each task has an owner and a due date.
- **Speed.** A sequenced checklist removes the "what's next" delays that stretch the close.
- **Auditability.** A documented, checked-off close is easier to review and defend.


## **The month-end close checklist template**


Organize the checklist into five phases, roughly in order. Adapt the specifics to your business, but the structure holds for most teams.


### **Phase 1: Pre-close preparation**


- Confirm the close calendar and owners for each task.
- Ensure all sub-ledgers (AR, AP, payroll, fixed assets) are up to date.
- Cut off and confirm all transactions for the period.
- Collect outstanding invoices, expense reports, and receipts.
- Verify bank feeds and data integrations are current.


### **Phase 2: Reconciliations**


- Reconcile all bank accounts to the general ledger. See[bank reconciliation](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/automate-bank-reconciliation) .
- Reconcile balance-sheet accounts (cash, AR, AP, prepaids, accruals). See[balance sheet reconciliation](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/balance-sheet-reconciliation) .
- Reconcile credit card and expense accounts.
- Reconcile intercompany balances and eliminations.
- Investigate and resolve any discrepancies.


### **Phase 3: Journal entries and adjustments**


- Record accruals for expenses incurred but not yet invoiced.
- Record deferrals and prepaid expense amortization.
- Record depreciation and amortization.
- Record payroll and benefits accruals.
- Post any correcting or reclassification entries.
- Review and approve all journal entries.


### **Phase 4: Review and close**


- Review the adjusted trial balance for accuracy.
- Run variance and flux analysis against prior period and budget. See[variance analysis](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/variance-analysis) .
- Investigate and explain significant variances.
- Obtain sign-offs from reviewers and the controller.
- Lock the period in the accounting system.


### **Phase 5: Reporting**


- Prepare the financial statements (income statement, balance sheet, cash flow).
- Prepare management and board reporting with commentary.
- Distribute reporting to stakeholders.
- Document the close and note issues to improve next period.


## **Tasks teams most often miss**


- **Flux commentary, not just flux numbers.** Explaining the "why" behind variances, not just flagging them.
- **Intercompany eliminations.** Easy to overlook in multi-entity closes and a common source of errors.
- **Accrual completeness.** Expenses incurred late in the period that have not been invoiced yet.
- **A post-close retro.** Noting what slowed the close so it improves next month.


## **How AI agents run the close checklist**

## **Frequently asked questions**


### **What is a month-end close checklist?**


A month-end close checklist is a structured list of the tasks required to close the books each period, organized by phase (preparation, reconciliations, journal entries, review, and reporting) with owners and due dates. It keeps the close consistent, accountable, and on time.


### **What are the steps in a month-end close?**


Pre-close preparation (cutoffs, sub-ledgers, data), reconciliations (bank, balance-sheet, intercompany), journal entries and adjustments (accruals, deferrals, depreciation), review and close (trial balance, variance analysis, sign-off, locking the period), and reporting (financial statements and management reporting).


### **How long should a month-end close take?**


It varies, but many teams target a close within five business days, and high-performing or automated teams close faster. A good checklist plus automation of reconciliations and entries is what compresses the timeline.


### **Can AI do the month-end close?**


AI agents can run much of the close, reconciliations, draft entries, variance analysis, and reporting, with a human reviewing and approving. The checklist still structures the work, but agents do the recurring tasks so the team reviews rather than executes from scratch.


## **The bottom line**


A month-end close checklist turns the close into a repeatable, accountable process: five phases, from pre-close prep through reporting, each with clear owners and tasks. Use the template above as a starting point, adapt it to your business, and watch for the tasks teams miss.
